sections.heading: From Naval Base to Freeport Zone
paragraphs: Subic Bay, about 100km northwest of Manila Bay, was formerly home to U.S. Naval Base Subic Bay -- one of the largest American overseas military installations -- until the U.S. Navy officially departed in 1992. [2] The area has since transformed into the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, an industrial and commercial hub attracting investment, tourism and economic development under the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority. That gives a race here a genuinely different backdrop than a typical city-centre leg -- wide former military roads and a mix of industrial and natural coastal scenery.

sections.heading: A Municipality With Its Own Identity
paragraphs: Subic itself is a municipality in Zambales province, with a 2024 census population of 116,788. [2] The name derives from the native Zambales word Hubek ('head of a plough'), later mispronounced by Spanish missionaries as Subiq -- a small but genuine piece of local etymology behind the modern Freeport Zone's name.
